purpose: Compose the already-reviewed Fulfillment migration-baseline reuse with the already-approved eight-shard functional workflow. UUID/data isolation, real rollback and cleanup, original global/per-file coverage and P1/P2 gates remain required.
data: Existing framework schema, migration seeds and ledger. Same synthetic case data, row counts and fault scenarios. One in-memory logical dump per participating test-file process and one restore into each subsequent fresh database.
concurrency: Eight existing independent MySQL server shards approved in #330. Tests remain serial within each shard; each fixture creates its own UUID database and connections. Snapshot cache is local to each test-file Node process.
repetitions: Each functional test file executes once in its existing assigned shard. No added cases, data, test repetitions, runner jobs or dispatches relative to the eight-shard main.
thresholds: All existing functional and rollback assertions. Server coverage lines/branches/functions 92/83/90 percent, original per-file floors, client coverage and aggregate/evidence gates. Observe natural PR first results against mean <= 10 minutes and maximum <= 15 minutes.
trigger: Existing admitted PR, main push, schedule and functional dispatch routes. Existing capacity exclusions apply. Optimization activates only for GITHUB_JOB=server-tests and SALES_CAPACITY_SEPARATE_STEP=1; the subsequent real P1/P2 browser step follows its existing fixture path.
cost: No new runner or job relative to eight-shard main. Participating test-file processes perform one logical dump before case data; subsequent fixture calls restore into fresh UUID databases. Existing four-shard evidence shows functional safety, but incremental speed and peak memory on the eight-shard composition are unmeasured. Use the normal approved PR/main runs; no load test or extra sample runs.
